title: Candle Anatomy
hook: Body, wicks, open, close. Know every part before you read a single chart.

launchpad.outcome: Name every part of a candle and know which one shows acceptance.
launchpad.missionQuestion: Which part of a candle actually shows what price accepted — the wick, or the close?

slides.kicker: The full anatomy of one candle
slides.body:
Every candle has four prices: open (where it started), close (where it ended — the one that matters most), high (the top of its full range), and low (the bottom).

The body is the distance between open and close — a bigger body means a more decisive move. The wick is everywhere price reached but didn't close — it shows travel, not acceptance.

slides.title: Tap the part that fits each clue
slides.intro: Same candle, unlabeled this time. Let's test what you just read — one part at a time.

rounds.prompt: Tap the part that shows price traveled somewhere but did NOT close there.

points.label: The wick
points.feedback: Exactly — that thin line above the body is the wick. Price reached up there but closed lower — it didn't hold.

points.label: The body
points.feedback: The body is the open-to-close range — that's what price DID hold, not what it reached and gave back.

points.label: The close
points.feedback: That's right at the edge where price settled — the close. We're looking for the part that reached but didn't stay.

rounds.prompt: Now tap the part that shows the distance between open and close.

points.label: The body
points.feedback: Exactly — the wide filled rectangle is the body, the open-to-close range.

points.label: The top wick
points.feedback: That thin line above is the wick, not the body — the body is the wider rectangle in the middle.

points.label: The bottom wick
points.feedback: That's the wick below the body — travel, not the body itself.

rounds.prompt: Last one — tap the highest price this candle reached.

points.label: The high
points.feedback: Right — that's the very top of the candle, the highest price reached this candle.

points.label: The low
points.feedback: That's the low — the bottom of the range, not the top.

points.label: The body
points.feedback: That's the body — we're looking for the highest point reached, at the very top of the wick.

slides.quote: A wick shows me where price went. A close shows me where price accepted. Read a candle in that order — body, then wicks, then respect the close.

slides.prompt: Imagine another AGHF member asks: "What's the difference between a wick and a close?" How would you explain it to them?
slides.modelAnswer: A wick shows me where price traveled but didn't stay — it's the reach. A close shows me where price actually settled, what the market accepted by the end of that candle. If I only look at the wick, I only know where price visited. The close tells me what actually held.

takeaways: The body is open-to-close distance; the wick is the reach that didn't hold.
A wick shows where price traveled; a close shows where price accepted.
Reading a candle cleanly means: body, then wicks, then close.
remember: A wick shows me where price went. A close shows me where price accepted.
